# octoqlgen configuration

`octoqlgen.yaml` is octoqlgen's only user-facing configuration file.

Run `go run github.com/willabides/octoql/cmd/octoqlgen@<version> init` to pin
and fetch the latest GitHub Docs `fpt` schema. Pass `--schema-version ghec`,
or a version such as `--schema-version ghes-3.21`, to initialize another
GitHub Docs schema. Then run generation, normally through a `go:generate`
directive. Pass `--config PATH` when the file is not named `octoqlgen.yaml`.

Every path and glob in this file resolves relative to the configuration file
itself, not to the current working directory.

This page is a catalog of every available option. It is not a template to
copy wholesale: many options below are alternatives to one another, and most
projects need only `schema`, `operations`, and `generated`. Run
`octoqlgen init` to produce a working starting configuration.

## `schema`

Type: `object` · Required

The local GraphQL schema, in SDL format, together with the optional
remote source it is pinned to.

`schema.path` is always the schema used for generation. Schema fetching
verifies an existing file, or downloads a missing file from the pinned
source. Generation performs the same verification or fetch before it
writes code.

Omit `schema.source` for a local-only schema. In that case `schema.sha256`
is optional, and is verified when present.

### `schema.path`

Type: `string` · Required

The path where the schema is read or materialized, relative to
`octoqlgen.yaml`.

Keep this in the gitignored `.octoql` directory when the source is
remote, so the reviewed pin in `octoqlgen.yaml` is the committed
artifact rather than the schema itself.

Example: `.octoql/schema.graphql`

### `schema.sha256`

Type: `string` · Optional

The SHA-256 digest of the schema bytes.

This is required for GitHub.com sources, where it is the exact digest
of the fetched file. It is optional for a local-only schema, and is
verified when present.

`octoqlgen schema update` rewrites this value along with
`schema.source.revision`.

Example: `c98cb9edeedd1fb56c8678c19a8ad540c8d0739dd94579dfedbe044192e4ab18`

### `schema.source`

Type: `object` · Optional

The GitHub.com repository, revision, and path the schema is fetched from.

Fetching requires GitHub authentication through `GH_TOKEN`,
`GITHUB_TOKEN`, or `gh auth token`.

#### `schema.source.repository`

Type: `string` · Required

The GitHub.com repository holding the schema, in `owner/name` form.

Example: `octo-org/octo-repo`

#### `schema.source.revision`

Type: `string` · Required

The full commit SHA pinning the schema.

`octoqlgen schema update` fetches the latest version of the
configured repository path from its default branch and rewrites this
value along with `schema.sha256`.

Example: `45d83f459620340069df7c375a8867be62616d61`

#### `schema.source.path`

Type: `string` · Required

The path to the schema file within the repository.

Example: `schema/github.graphql`

## `operations`

Type: `array` · Required

Filenames or globs holding the operations to generate code for, relative
to `octoqlgen.yaml`.

These may be `.graphql` files containing operations in SDL form, or Go
files, in which case any string literal starting with (optional
whitespace and) the string `# @octoqlgen` is extracted as an operation.

Operations are always written as a list, even when only one path is
needed.

Query and mutation names become generated helper names, so an operation
needs an uppercase name whenever its helper must be exported.
Subscriptions are not supported and are rejected.

Example: `graphql/**/*.graphql`

## `generated`

Type: `string` · Required

The file to write the generated client to, relative to `octoqlgen.yaml`.

The generated client is self-contained. It uses only the standard library
unless configured bindings add imports, and application code never
imports `github.com/willabides/octoql`.

Example: `githubapi/generated.go`

## `package`

Type: `string` · Optional

The package name for the generated code. Defaults to the package name
corresponding to the directory of `generated`.

This is rarely needed: only when the package name must differ from the
suffix of the package path, and there are no other Go files in the
package already.

Example: `githubapi`

## `export_operations`

Type: `string` · Optional

When set, a file at this path (relative to `octoqlgen.yaml`) is generated
containing the exact operations octoql sends to the server.

This is useful for servers that require operations to be explicitly
safelisted, especially for cases like operations involving fragments
where the sent document may not exactly match the input, and for other
static analysis. The JSON is an object of the form:

```json
{"operations": [{
  "operationName": "operationname",
  "query": "query operationName { ... }",
  "sourceLocation": "myqueriesfile.graphql"
}]}
```

Keys may be added in the future. By default no such file is written.

Example: `operations.json`

## `context_type`

Type: `string` · Optional

The fully qualified name of a Go type that generated helpers accept and
use as the `context.Context` for HTTP requests.

Defaults to `context.Context`. Set it to `-` to omit the context argument
entirely, in which case generated helpers use `context.Background()`. Any
other value must be a type that implements `context.Context`.

Example: `context.Context`

## `bindings`

Type: `object` · Optional

A map from GraphQL type name to Go type, overriding the Go type octoqlgen
would otherwise use for that GraphQL type.

This is primarily used for custom scalars, or to map builtin scalars to a
nonstandard type defined elsewhere. By default, builtin scalars map to
the obvious Go types: `String` and `ID` to `string`, `Int` to `int`,
`Float` to `float64`, and `Boolean` to `bool`.

octoql also maps several GitHub scalars by default. `DateTime`,
`PreciseDateTime`, and `GitTimestamp` map to `time.Time`.
`CustomPropertyValue` maps to `encoding/json.RawMessage`, because GitHub
may return either a string or an array of strings. `Base64String`,
`BigInt`, `Date`, `GitObjectID`, `GitRefname`, `GitSSHRemote`, `HTML`,
`URI`, and `X509Certificate` map to `string`. This setting extends or
overrides all of those mappings.

octoqlgen does not validate bound types in any way. They must define
whatever logic is needed, such as `MarshalJSON`/`UnmarshalJSON` methods or
JSON tags, to convert to and from JSON. For this reason binding object,
interface, or union types is not recommended, because nothing guarantees
that the fields requested in the operation match those present in the Go
type.

When binding to types in the same package as the generated code, take
care not to bind to generated types, or the result is circular.

To get equivalent behavior for a single operation, use
`@octoqlgen(bind: ...)`. See the directive reference. See also
`@octoqlgen(typename: ...)`, which maps a builtin scalar to a nonstandard
type that octoqlgen defines for you.

A single entry in `bindings`, describing the Go type to use for one
GraphQL type and how to convert it to and from JSON.

### `bindings.<name>.type`

Type: `string` · Optional

The fully qualified name of the Go type to bind to, for example
`time.Time`, `map[string]interface{}`, or
`github.com/you/yourpkg/subpkg.MyType`.

This may be any of the following expressions:

- any named type, qualified by the full package path
- any predeclared basic type, such as `string` or `int`
- `interface{}`
- for any allowed type `T`: `*T`, `[]T`, `[N]T`, and `map[string]T`

It may not be an inline (unnamed) struct or interface type, a map
whose key type is not `string`, or a nonstandard spelling of those,
such as `interface {/* hi */}` or `map[  string      ]T`.

Example: `time.Time`

### `bindings.<name>.expect_exact_fields`

Type: `string` · Optional

A GraphQL selection that must exactly match the fields requested
wherever this type is used. Only applies when the GraphQL type is a
composite output type: an object, interface, or union.

This is useful when the bound type is a struct whose `UnmarshalJSON`
or other methods expect that certain fields were requested. For
example, with `expect_exact_fields: "{ id name }"`, octoqlgen rejects
the selection `{ fieldOfMyType { id title } }`.

Fields must match exactly, including ordering, so `{ name id }` is
also rejected. Arguments and directives, if any, need not match.

Example: `{ id name }`

### `bindings.<name>.marshaler`

Type: `string` · Optional

The fully qualified name of the function to use when marshaling this
type.

This is useful when binding to a standard type but using nonstandard
marshaling, for example when making requests to a server that is not
compatible with Go's default time format. It is only used for values
passed as arguments: input types, scalars, and enums.

The function should have a signature similar to `json.Marshal`. It is
passed one argument, a pointer to a value of the given type, and
returns the JSON as a `[]byte` and an error:

```go
func MarshalMyType(v *MyType) ([]byte, error)
```

The `omitempty` option is ignored for types with custom marshalers. A
custom marshaler can encode `"null"`, but that sends an explicit
GraphQL null rather than omitting the variable.

The default is ordinary JSON marshaling.

Example: `github.com/you/yourpkg.MarshalMyType`

### `bindings.<name>.unmarshaler`

Type: `string` · Optional

The fully qualified name of the function to use when unmarshaling this
type.

The function should have a signature similar to `json.Unmarshal`. It
is passed a `[]byte` of JSON and a pointer to a value of the given
type, and returns an error:

```go
func UnmarshalMyType(b []byte, v *MyType) error
```

The default is ordinary JSON unmarshaling.

Example: `github.com/you/yourpkg.UnmarshalMyType`

## `package_bindings`

Type: `array` · Optional

A list of packages for which octoqlgen automatically generates bindings.

This is equivalent to adding an entry to `bindings` mapping each exported
type in the package to its own name:

```yaml
bindings:
  TypeName:
    type: github.com/you/yourpkg/models.TypeName
```

Multiple packages may be specified, and later ones take precedence over
earlier ones. Explicit entries in `bindings` take precedence over all
package bindings.

Take care that this is not the package holding the generated code, or the
result is circular.

A single entry in `package_bindings`.

### `package_bindings[].package`

Type: `string` · Required

The import path of the package whose exported types become bindings.

Example: `github.com/you/yourpkg/models`

## `casing`

Type: `object` · Optional

By default octoqlgen converts GraphQL names to Go style automatically.
Sometimes that does not produce the desired result; these options
configure the algorithm for a given schema.

Each option accepts one of the following values:

- `default`: use octoqlgen's default algorithm, which converts GraphQL
  names to exported Go names. This is usually best for schemas using
  idiomatic GraphQL naming.
- `raw`: map the GraphQL name exactly, without converting it to Go style.
  This is usually best for schemas with casing conflicts, such as enums
  whose values differ only in casing.
- `auto_camel_case`: convert `snake_case` to `camelCase` before standard
  processing. This applies to field names, type names, and enum values.

### `casing.default`

Type: `string` · Optional

The casing algorithm to use for all GraphQL names, including fields
and types.

Example: `auto_camel_case`

### `casing.all_enums`

Type: `string` · Optional

The casing algorithm to use for all GraphQL enum values.

Example: `raw`

### `casing.enums`

Type: `object` · Optional

The casing algorithm to use for the values of specific GraphQL enum
types. These entries take precedence over `all_enums`.

## `use_struct_references`

Type: `boolean` · Optional

When true, fields with a struct type default to `pointer: true` and
`omitempty: true`.

This is useful for schemas where it would be burdensome to set those
options manually on a large number of fields. Defaults to false.

Example: `true`

## `omit_unreferenced_implementations`

Type: `boolean` · Optional

Generate concrete Go structs only for the abstract GraphQL
implementations named by applicable inline or named fragments.

Each abstract selection also gets an `OctoqlOther` catch-all containing
the shared fields and `__typename`, so responses remain usable when
GitHub returns another current or future implementation.

Defaults to true. Set it to false when migrating code that relies on a
generated Go struct for every implementation allowed by the schema.

Example: `true`

## `test_handler`

Type: `object` · Optional

Generate an optional typed GraphQL test handler from the same parsed
operation plan used for the client.

The handler package is inferred independently from its destination,
including when the destination directory is new and empty.

Every test-handler operation name must begin with an uppercase letter.
This applies to both type strategies; `local` does not relax it.

Omitting `test_handler` generates only the client and performs no handler
package work.

### `test_handler.generated`

Type: `string` · Required

The file to write the generated test handler to, relative to
`octoqlgen.yaml`. Required whenever `test_handler` is present.

Example: `githubapitest/generated.go`

### `test_handler.types`

Type: `string` · Optional · Default: `client` · Values: `client`, `local`

Where the handler's operation types come from.

`client`, the default, imports the generated client package and
exposes aliases for its response, input, enum, abstract variant, and
`OctoqlOther` types. Handler response values are then assignable to
generated client types. Because another package aliases the generated
client operation types, this also requires exported operation names.

`local` emits distinct but wire-equivalent operation types directly in
the handler package, without importing the client. Local values are
not directly assignable to client types. In this mode reachable
binding types and marshal helpers may be external or owned by the
handler package, but may not be owned by the generated client
package, because that would reintroduce the client dependency.
